headline: Attackers are exploiting two unpatched remote code execution zero-days in Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway, and Citrix has published neither a confirmation nor a fix.

emerging_trends.text: Edge appliances keep failing first, with attackers running two unpatched NetScaler zero-days over the weekend days after CISA cataloged live exploitation of MikroTik RouterOS and Microsoft SharePoint, which makes perimeter gear the fastest route into an enterprise.

emerging_trends.topic_title: Scareware Ads and the Macfinger ClickFix Campaign

emerging_trends.text: Defenders keep measuring coverage they do not have: Conifers found that 47 percent of detection rules in the average organization need attention, and CISA's new election plan names patching barriers as a top obstacle for state and county systems.

topics.title: SharePoint Exploitation Puts Agencies on a Monday Deadline
topics.latest_developments: SecurityWeek reported on September 27, 2026 that attackers now exploit CVE-2026-65660 in the wild, and the CISA patching deadline for federal agencies falls Monday, September 28, 2026.
topics.summary: CVE-2026-65660, rated 8.8, is a code injection flaw in Microsoft Office SharePoint Server that gives an authenticated user remote code execution; CISA listed it alongside CVE-2026-67279 in MikroTik RouterOS. Patch both, and treat any internet-facing SharePoint server as a priority.

sources.title: Microsoft SharePoint Flaw CVE-2026-65660 Now Exploited in Attacks
SharePoint RCE and MikroTik RouterOS Flaws Actively Exploited in the Wild

topics.title: Citrix NetScaler Zero-Days Under Active Exploitation
topics.latest_developments: The security firm watchTowr reported on September 26, 2026 that attackers exploit two unpatched remote code execution zero-days in Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway appliances, and some administrators have pulled their appliances off the network rather than wait for a fix.
topics.summary: NetScaler ADC and Gateway terminate remote access and load-balance applications for enterprises worldwide, and remote code execution on one hands an attacker the network edge. Citrix has confirmed nothing and shipped nothing; take the appliances offline or lock down their management interfaces until a patch arrives.

sources.title: Warning: Two Unpatched Citrix NetScaler RCE Zero-Days Under Active Exploitation

topics.title: Scareware Ads and the Macfinger ClickFix Campaign
topics.latest_developments: Ars Technica reported on September 25, 2026 that Google ad placements across the internet deliver scareware that freezes a Mac and tells its owner the machine carries an infection, and the SANS Internet Storm Center published a breakdown of the malware behind the Macfinger ClickFix campaign the same day.
topics.summary: Both routes convince the person at the keyboard to act: the ad fakes an infection warning, and ClickFix lures hand the victim a command to paste. Train staff to treat any browser page claiming an infection as hostile, and block the paste-and-run pattern at the endpoint.

sources.title: Your uncle's frozen Mac says it's infected after viewing a Google ad. Now what?
A Closer Look at Malware From the Macfinger ClickFix Campaign, (Fri, Sep 25th)

topics.title: A Cyberattack Disrupts Dyfed-Powys Police
topics.latest_developments: Dyfed-Powys Police, the force covering southwest and mid Wales, said on September 25, 2026 that a cyberattack knocked out some of its non-emergency systems and may have exposed staff information.
topics.summary: The force kept emergency response running while it worked through the outage and assessed what attackers reached. Police staff records carry home addresses and personal details that make officers targets, so the exposure question matters more than the downtime.

sources.title: Cyberattack hits Welsh police force, may have affected staff data

topics.title: CISA Delivers an Election Security Plan
topics.latest_developments: CISA published the election security plan that Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin ordered in July 2026, and it flags attacks on voter registration databases and the barriers that keep election offices from patching their systems.
topics.summary: State and county election offices run the machinery of American voting on small budgets and thin staff, which leaves known vulnerabilities open for months. The plan sets out what the agency will do about both problems ahead of the next federal election cycle.

sources.title: CISA Election Security Plan Flags Patching Barriers, Voter Database Attacks

topics.title: Conifers Finds Detection Rules Failing Quietly
topics.latest_developments: Conifers assessed 14,652 detection rules across its customer base and found that 47 percent of the detections in the average organization need attention, with failures falling into five groups that start with logic bugs.
topics.summary: The study covered rules customers wrote themselves and rules vendors manage inside SIEM, endpoint, cloud, identity, email, and network tools. A rule can show as deployed on a coverage dashboard and still never fire when an attacker uses the technique it targets, so test detections against real technique execution instead of trusting the dashboard.

sources.title: Threat detection dashboards are masking security coverage gaps

business_politics.title: Explosives Arrests at the British Base Flying Iran Strikes
business_politics.latest_developments: Police in western England arrested several men Sunday, September 27, on suspicion of explosives offenses near RAF Fairford, the Royal Air Force base the United States Air Force has used to launch strikes on Iran, and counter-terrorism officers took over the investigation.
business_politics.summary: RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire hosts American bombers running missions in the seven-month war with Iran, and British police declared a major incident and evacuated homes around the perimeter. An attack attempt on the launch point for American strikes carries the war onto British soil.

sources.title: Explosives arrests made in ‘major incident’ near RAF Fairford

business_politics.title: Swiss Voters Rule on Neutrality
business_politics.latest_developments: Switzerland votes Sunday, September 27, on a measure that would bar the country from cooperating with any military alliance unless an enemy attacks it first.
business_politics.summary: The referendum would write centuries of Swiss neutrality into a hard constitutional rule, cutting off the quiet defense cooperation Bern has built with European partners since Russia invaded Ukraine. A Yes vote would lock Switzerland out of joint procurement, air-defense coordination, and NATO-adjacent exercises for the duration of any conflict it does not directly enter.

sources.title: Swiss voters to decide fate of centuries-old neutrality policy

business_politics.title: Private Credit Redemptions Slow
business_politics.latest_developments: Redemption requests from retail investors in private credit funds fell, the Financial Times reported Sunday, September 27, easing the withdrawal pressure that had built through the summer, though fund managers told the paper it remains too early to call the bottom.
business_politics.summary: Retail money in semi-liquid private credit vehicles had been heading for the exits, forcing managers to meet redemptions out of a portfolio of loans that trade rarely. A slower pace of withdrawals relieves the funding mismatch that banks lending into the sector watch most closely.

sources.title: Private credit turmoil eases as investor withdrawals slow

business_politics.title: Europe and Asia Head Into an LNG Bidding War
business_politics.latest_developments: The Financial Times reported Sunday, September 27, that European Union gas storage sits at record lows heading into winter, setting up intensifying competition with Asian buyers for liquefied natural gas cargoes over the coming months.
business_politics.summary: The war with Iran and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz have thinned the pool of seaborne cargoes just as Europe enters the heating season with its tanks emptier than at any point on record. Every cargo Asia outbids Europe for pushes European gas and power prices higher and squeezes energy-intensive industry, which has already idled plants in Britain.

sources.title: Europe braces for LNG tug of war with Asia

business.title: CCAC Faculty Rally Over Their Contract
business.latest_developments: Community College of Allegheny County faculty members rallied Saturday, September 26, at the college's North Side campus as contract negotiations with the administration continue.
business.summary: CCAC runs four campuses across Allegheny County and enrolls the region's largest body of two-year students. The faculty took their bargaining fight outdoors on the North Side the same weekend the college marked its 60th year.

sources.title: CCAC faculty rally at North Side campus amid contract negotiations

business.title: Washington County Opens a Flood Recovery Center
business.latest_developments: Washington County will host a Multi-Agency Response Center to help residents and business owners recover from the storm damage and flooding of the past two weekends, WPXI reported Sunday, September 27.
business.summary: Two straight weekends of heavy rain pushed Chartiers Creek and other streams over their banks, swamping buildings along Jefferson Avenue in Canton Township and prompting the township to declare a state of emergency on September 20. The response center gathers aid agencies in one place so flooded households and businesses can file damage claims and reach recovery programs without chasing them separately.

sources.title: Washington County floods: Response center to aid residents, businesses recovering from storm damage

around_town.title: The Cathedral of Learning Turns 100
around_town.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette published two pieces Sunday, September 27, marking the centennial of the University of Pittsburgh's Cathedral of Learning, one tracing how the tower became a Pittsburgh landmark and one collecting readers' memories of the building they call Cathy.
around_town.summary: The Gothic skyscraper anchors Pitt's Oakland campus, holds the Nationality Rooms, and serves as classroom space and civic symbol at once. The anniversary lands as Pitt runs the $3 billion "Proving Possible" fundraising campaign it opened September 25.

sources.title: How Pitt's Cathedral of Learning has remained a beacon in Pittsburgh as it hits 100

around_town.title: The Races That Decide Harrisburg
around_town.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette laid out Sunday, September 27, the specific 2026 legislative contests that will determine which party controls the Pennsylvania House and Senate, with the election five weeks off on November 3.
around_town.summary: Democrats hold the Pennsylvania House by a single seat and Republicans hold the Senate, so a handful of suburban and Western Pennsylvania districts decide whether Governor Josh Shapiro governs with a split legislature or a friendlier one. Allegheny County mailed roughly 120,000 ballots to voters starting last weekend.

sources.title: The 2026 races that could decide control of the Pennsylvania House and Senate

around_town.title: The Nor'easter Sends Clouds and Little Else
around_town.latest_developments: WPXI, WTAE, and KDKA all forecast Sunday morning, September 27, that the nor'easter backing inland will hold most of its rain east of the region, leaving Pittsburgh cloudy and breezy with seasonable temperatures and a chance of light rain by evening.
around_town.summary: The Laurel Highlands ridges carry the best shower chance through the day. Kickoff at Acrisure Stadium at 1 p.m. falls inside the dry stretch.

sources.title: Clouds increase as nor’easter moves inland; little rain expected in Pittsburgh region
Western PA: Cloudy and breezy with few light showers
Seasonable temperatures remain in Pittsburgh on Sunday with some light rain possible

around_teams.title: The Tight End Case Against Cincinnati
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette's scouting report, published Sunday morning, September 27, argues that head coach Mike McCarthy should follow the league-wide turn toward tight ends against the Cincinnati Bengals, and Gerry Dulac released his Week 3 picks the same morning.
around_teams.summary: The Steelers open AFC North play against the undefeated Bengals at 1 p.m. Sunday at Acrisure Stadium on CBS, carrying the NFL's worst offense into the game with running back Rico Dowdle hurt and rookie lineman Gennings Dunker on injured reserve. Pat Freiermuth gives McCarthy the piece the Post-Gazette says the passing game has underused through two weeks.

sources.title: Steelers-Bengals scouting report: It’s time for Mike McCarthy to hop on the tight end trend
Gerry Dulac’s 2026 NFL predictions: Week 3

team_usa.title: Eleven Debuts in a 4-1 Win Over Peru
team_usa.latest_developments: ESPN reported Sunday, September 27, that Mauricio Pochettino handed out 11 debuts in the United States' 4-1 win over Peru in Orlando, Florida, eight of them to teenagers, and that the coach called himself "so proud" and said the play gave him goosebumps.
team_usa.summary: The friendly Saturday, September 26, was the American men's first match since the 2026 World Cup and the opening of the cycle toward 2030. Sebastian Berhalter drew a 10 and Justin Ellis a 9 in ESPN's player ratings, and 16-year-old Cavan Sullivan started, the youngest American to do so since Freddy Adu in 2006.

sources.title: Poch 'so proud' as 8 teens debut in USMNT rout
USMNT player ratings: Ellis gets 9, Berhalter 10 in Peru rout
There's a palpable sense of excitement surrounding the USMNT's young guns
